Note::NlpAccessor::remove_html¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note Note::NlpAccessor::remove_html() const

Strip Markup While Retaining Visible Text¶

remove_html() removes element-like markup and comments while preserving text between tags. It is useful when markup supplies presentation or document structure but the next operation needs plain textual content. It does not decode entities, execute a document model, or validate nesting; use html_unescape() separately when encoded entities such as &amp; should become their represented characters.

The lexical recognizer handles these forms:

Form

Example

Result

Opening and closing elements

<strong>text</strong>

Tags removed; text retained

Elements with attributes

<a href="/x">link</a>

Tags removed; link retained

Self-closing elements

<br/>, <item key="x" />

Element removed

Closed comments

<!-- internal -->

Comment and its contents removed

Declarations

<!DOCTYPE html>

Declaration removed

Processing instructions

<?xml version="1.0"?>

Instruction removed

Named or namespaced elements

<x-card>, <svg:path>

Tag removed

An ordinary element name must begin immediately after < or </ with an ASCII letter. This protects comparison-like prose such as 3 < 5 and x < y > z; < b > is likewise not treated as an element. Because this is a bounded lexical cleanup rather than a full parser, malformed or unclosed constructs are not repaired, script/style semantics are not interpreted, and matching tags are not required to balance before recognized tag spans are removed.

After an actual removal, ASCII whitespace is collapsed and stripped. A space introduced immediately before ., ,, ;, :, !, ?, ), or ] is removed, so closing markup does not turn world. into world .. Text from adjacent block elements remains separated rather than being concatenated into one word. If nothing matches, the input cell is returned byte-for-byte.

The result is a fresh Text Note with unchanged rank and shape. Empty visible content becomes an empty cell, not absence. Applying the operation twice is idempotent for the recognized grammar. Undefined Notes remain undefined, empty Notes remain empty, and Bytes, Bool, Int64, and Float64 Notes reject. Cells missing either < or > take a fast path that avoids regex processing.

Example 1: Elements, Comments, Punctuation, And Entities¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({
        "<p>Hello <strong>world</strong>.</p>"
        "<!-- hidden --><div>Tail &amp; more</div>"})
        .nlp().remove_html()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["Hello world. Tail &amp; more"]

The comment disappears with its contents, visible element text survives, the period remains attached to world, and &amp; remains encoded by design.

Example 2: Declarations And Custom Elements¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({
        "<!DOCTYPE html><?xml version=\"1.0\"?>"
        "<x-card data-id=\"7\">Value</x-card>"})
        .nlp().remove_html()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["Value"]

This demonstrates lexical support beyond the small set of built-in element names; the operation recognizes element syntax rather than maintaining a tag allow-list.

Example 3: Adjacent Blocks Keep A Word Boundary¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"<div>One</div><div>Two</div>"})
        .nlp().remove_html()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["One Two"]

Example 4: Comparison Text Is An Exact No-Op¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"  3 < 5 and x < y > z\nstill text  "})
        .nlp().remove_html()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["  3 < 5 and x < y > z\nstill text  "]

No tag was recognized, so whitespace normalization is not applied as an unrelated side effect.

Example 5: Higher-Rank Notes Retain Their Structure¶

const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"a@b.io", "Page 1", "#tag", "<b>bold</b>"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(matrix.nlp().remove_html()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["a@b.io", "Page 1"], 
  ["#tag", "bold"]
]

Only the fourth cell contains recognized markup; every coordinate and extent remain unchanged.

Example 6: Empty, Undefined, And Non-Text Contracts¶

const auto empty = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{}, std::array<std::int64_t, 1>{0});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(empty.nlp().remove_html()) << '\n';

const pluss::Note undefined;
std::cout << "undefined defined=" << std::boolalpha
          << undefined.nlp().remove_html().defined() << '\n';

try {
  (void)pluss::note::bytes({std::byte{0x3c}}).nlp().remove_html();
} catch (const std::exception&) {
  std::cout << "Bytes: rejected\n";
}

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]
undefined defined=false
Bytes: rejected

Bool, Int64, and Float64 Notes reject under the same Text-only rule.
